How the International Team are closing on history but have a big final day ahead at Medinah; watch the Sunday singles live from 4.30pm on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 27 September 2026 07:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the third day of the 2026 Presidents Cup, where the International Team moved closer to a famous win on American soil Brandt Snedeker has given a self-critical assessment of his own Presidents Cup captaincy so far, with time quickly running out to avoid an embarrassing defeat for Team USA on home soil. Team USA came into the week as overwhelming favourites to claim a record-extending 11th consecutive victory, in a biennial event where much of the pre-tournament narrative was around whether change was needed to make it more competitive. Next to no hope had been given to Geoff Ogilvy's International Team, who earned their only Presidents Cup win in 1998 and have lost every edition since a 17-17 tie in 2003, but they are now five points away from completing a seismic shock at Medinah. metadata.content: George Russell: Is Mercedes driver really back after 'Grand Slam' Azerbaijan GP win cut Kimi Antonelli's F1 title lead? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis George Russell: Is Mercedes driver really back after 'Grand Slam' Azerbaijan GP win cut Kimi Antonelli's F1 title lead? George Russell produced the most statistically complete weekend of his Formula 1 career to win the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, but did the performance confirm the Brit is back to his best? Russell drove superbly in Baku to claim the first Grand Slam of his career, taking pole position, leading from lights-to-flag on his way to victory, and setting the fastest lap of the race. The result saw Russell reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's lead at the top of the world championship to 66 points with eight rounds remaining, ensuring some intrigue remains as the season enters its closing stretch. metadata.summary: The International Team moved another step closer to a historic Presidents Cup win on American soil by taking a 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into the Sunday singles.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: International Team take historic 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into Sunday singles and chase Medinah win | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: International Team take historic 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into Sunday singles and chase Medinah win A tied afternoon foursomes sessions gave the International Team a three-point lead into the final day at Medinah; Internationals need five points from the Sunday singles to claim just their second Presidents Cup win ever; watch the Sunday singles live from 4.30pm on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 27 September 2026 00:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Saturday's double session at the Presidents Cup, where the Internationals continue to lead on away soil The International Team moved another step closer to a historic Presidents Cup win on American soil by taking a 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into the Sunday singles. Geoff Ogilvy's side held a four-point advantage after the first two days at Medinah Country Club, following their historic foursomes sessions sweep on Friday, then added 1.5 points from four matches during a tight Saturday fourballs session. Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker benched world No 1 Scottie Scheffler for the afternoon foursomes, where they threatened their own session sweep after grabbing the early lead in all four matches. metadata.summary: Roy Keane disagreed with Anthony Gordon's assessment that England are at the same level as Spain after the World Cup winners came from behind to beat Thomas Tuchel's side 3-2 in their Nations League opener.
metadata.content: England 2-3 Spain: Anthony Gordon and Roy Keane disagree over gap between Three Lions and world champions | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England 2-3 Spain: Anthony Gordon and Roy Keane disagree over gap between Three Lions and world champions World Cup winners Spain pounced on basic errors from England's Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly for their first two goals, while Thomas Tuchel's side failed to capitalise on their dominance with Harry Kane's missed penalty proving to be a turning point at Wembley Sunday 27 September 2026 08:20, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett and Pete Smith rate the England players' performances in the game against Spain Roy Keane disagreed with Anthony Gordon's assessment that England are at the same level as Spain after the World Cup winners came from behind to beat Thomas Tuchel's side 3-2 in their Nations League opener. Spain extend their unbeaten run to 39 games with the win at Wembley, but the game could have had a very different outcome had Harry Kane not missed a second-half penalty after he headed England 2-1 in front before the break. The momentum shifted in Spain's favour after Kane's slip, with Alex Baena equalising off the bench before setting up the winner, scored by fellow substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who broke England hearts in the Euro 2024 final.
